title: Introduce per-route residency enforcement, KMS-consent middleware, and immutable audit checkpoints
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Added per-route data residency enforcement and KMS-consent middleware; introduced immutable audit checkpointing and RBAC v2 binding adapter. Backwards-compatible config flags; rollout via feature flag 'residency_enforcer_v1'.
description:
Context: Customers increasingly require per-endpoint data residency guarantees and stronger audit proofing when KMS operations cross regions. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a per-route residency enforcement layer that validates route-level residency policies before request routing; 2) a KMS-consent middleware that surfaces explicit consent/consumption traces when a request would cause cross-region key usage; 3) an immutable audit checkpoint mechanism that signs and seals critical audit events with a cluster CMK and writes checkpoint references to the audit store. Motivation: close gaps where a request on a global route could inadvertently use a regionally-scoped CMK or be routed through an incompatible region without tenant consent. This improves compliance posture for geo-sensitive customers and enables certified audit trails for SOC/ISO work. Changes included (high level): - New config: service.routes[].residency_policy {allowed_regions, deny_cross_region, require_kms_consent} - Residency enforcement middleware in gateway/router that rejects or annotates requests based on route policy - KMS-consent middleware that injects consent tokens, records the consent event in the audit trail, and rejects requests when consent is required but absent - Audit checkpoint service: signs a compact checkpoint blob with cluster CMK, stores signed reference in audit-store, and emits a sealed_event marker to the audit stream - RBAC v2 adapter: small converter that maps existing service-account role bindings to the new attribute-driven checks used by the residency enforcer - Tests & infra: e2e tests, unit coverage for middleware, integration test with kms-emulator, and a performance microbenchmark to quantify latency impact on cold-paths Rollout and feature-flagging: This is gated behind feature.residency_enforcer_v1 (default off). The rollout plan in the PR description includes: canary 5% of requests to region-us-east-1, collect KPI: reject-rate, latency p95, audit store write latency, and KMS-op deltas. If metrics are stable, ramp to 100% in two-week windows. Checklist: - [x] API + config schema - [x] Residency enforcement middleware implemented - [x] KMS-consent middleware and consent token flow - [x] Immutable audit checkpoint signer and persistence - [x] RBAC v2 binding adapter (compat-mode) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] E2E with kms-emulator - [x] Documentation: config, rollout, troubleshooting - [x] Security review by SEC team

Commit summary: - feat(residency): add route policy schema and enforcement hooks - feat(kms-consent): implement consent token flow and audit emission - feat(audit): checkpoint signer that uses cluster CMK and exposes checkpoint API - chore(rbac): add compat adapter from legacy bindings to v2 attribute checks - test: add e2e and perf microbenchmarks - docs: add residenty.md and migration guide

Changed areas (high-level): - gateway/router/middleware/residency_enforcer.go - gateway/middleware/kms_consent.go - services/audit/checkpoint_signer.go - config/schemas/route_residency.yaml - rbac/adapter/legacy_to_v2_converter.go - tests/e2e/residency_canary_test.go - docs/security/residency.md - infra/ci/kms_emulator.yml - examples/route-policy-samples.yaml - helm/values.residency.example.yaml - internal/observability/metrics_residency.go - perf/bench/residency_coldpath_bench.go

Review conversation (excerpt): "Jordan Kim (reviewer): Why do we need a separate consent token instead of reusing existing audit headers?" Author reply: "Aisha Kapoor: We considered reusing x-audit-token but needed a tamper-resistant consent artifact that can be validated independently by downstream KMS proxies; consent tokens are short-lived and signed by the gateway to prevent replay. We still emit audit headers for correlation." "Lena Müller: Can this accidentally increase p95 for small requests?" Author reply: "Aisha Kapoor: We added a fast-path that skips signing when policy is allow-local and no cross-region operation is detected; the perf microbenchmark shows a median increase of 1.2ms on cold-paths and <0.2ms on warm-paths. We'll monitor during canary." "Ravi Patel: Is the checkpoint signer single-writer? What happens if signer fails?" Author reply: "Aisha Kapoor: The signer uses a leader-election-backed single-writer in hosted; fallback writes an unsigned provisional checkpoint with a retry loop and emits a diagnostic alert. Signed checkpoints are required for final audit ingestion; provisional ones are marked until re-signed." "SEC team (comment): Please ensure the CMK rotation plan and key access list are documented." Author reply: "Added KEY_ROTATION.md and scoped the signer to cluster CMK with ACLs; SEC approved on 2024-11-08." 

CI summary: - unit/tests: pass - integration/kms-emulator: pass - lint: pass - build: pass - e2e/residency_canary_test: pass - perf/bench: completed (bench run artifacts attached) Flaky checks: none.

Migration notes: - Existing route config without residency_policy is treated as allow-global (preserves current behavior). - We provide rbac/adapter/legacy_to_v2_converter to auto-generate suggested attribute bindings; maintainers should review generated bindings before enabling strict enforcement. - If you enable require_kms_consent on a route, clients must present consent tokens or requests will be rejected (400/consent_required). Troubleshooting: - diag/residency-rejects exposes reasons and matching policy; - audit/checkpoints expose last_signed_checkpoint_id and status; - gateway logs include consent token validation outcome.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Jordan, Lena, and Ravi and SEC signoff. CI green. Feature flag created and documented. Post-merge tasks: schedule rollout with SRE, add dashboard panels for reject-rate and checkpoint write latency, and add an entry to the next compliance audit checklist.
